heading: 10.04.010 When Open - Rules and Regulations Generally.
text:
The municipal swimming pools of the City shall be opened to the public as limited in this chapter at all proper and seasonable times subject to such rules and regulations contained in this chapter and as the Governing Body of the City may from time to time adopt or authorize and as provided by the rules and regulations of the Kansas State Board of Health.
(History: Ord. SP-518 §3, 68)

heading: 10.04.020 Manager and Employees - Duties Generally.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation, with the consent of the City Manager, shall appoint pool managers and other employees of the swimming pools. The pool managers shall have general supervision over the swimming pools and over all people attending the same and the park areas in which the same are located. It shall be the pool managers' duty to preserve order, to enforce all provisions of this chapter and the rules and regulations of the City and the Kansas State Board of Health, and the managers may exclude any person or persons from the pools, and their grounds for the violations of this chapter, such rules and regulations as may be made by the City or the Kansas State Board of Health or when the pool manager deems such exclusion to be in the best interest of the orderly and peaceable operation and management of the pools.
(History: Ord. SP-829 §1, 75; SP-518 §4, 68)

heading: 10.04.030 Maintenance of Order and Peace.
text:
It shall be the duty of the pool managers and/or the assistant pool managers of the City's swimming pools, or any police officer of this City to maintain order and keep the public peace within the City parks and swimming pools of the City.
(History: Ord. SP-518 §5, 68)

heading: 10.04.040 Contagious Diseases.
text:
It is unlawful and a violation of this chapter for any person or persons at any time to enter the waters of the swimming pools who are afflicted with any venereal, infectious or contagious disease. The manager of the pools appointed as provided in this chapter are authorized, directed and empowered within their discretion to require from any person requesting permission to enter the swimming pools, a certificate of health from a licensed doctor of medicine, with his general practice or his residence in the City, designated by the manager, dated within three days of the date admission is sought, stating that the person applying for admission to the pool is free from any infectious or contagious disease which might endanger the health of other occupants of the pool.
(History: Ord. SP-518 §6, 68)

heading: 10.04.050 When Admittance May Be Refused.
text:
The pool managers appointed as provided for in this chapter are authorized, directed and empowered to refuse admission to any person applying for admission to the pools who is known to be not of good moral character, intoxicated or under the influence of drugs or opiates, or any person having a skin disease, open sores or cuts. The pool manager may, when they deem the same to be in the best interest of orderly operation and management of the pools, refuse admission to any person or persons whatsoever.
(History: Ord. SP-518 §7, 68)

heading: 10.04.060 Pollution and Contamination Prohibited.
text:
It is unlawful for any person or persons to throw or place in the waters of the pools any stones, debris, refuse or discarded substances; it is further unlawful for any person in any manner willfully to pollute the waters of the pools.
(History: Ord. SP-518 §8, 68)

heading: 10.04.070 Animals Prohibited.
text:
Except for special events authorized by the Director of Parks and Recreation, it is unlawful at all times for any person or persons to place in the waters of the swimming pools, or cause or to suffer any dogs or any animals of any kind to enter or be therein.
(History: Ord. SP-2826 §1, 2009; SP-518 §9, 68)

heading: 10.04.080 Pool Hours - Unlawful Entrance.
text:
The hours during which the swimming pools are open for use shall be determined by the Director of Parks and Recreation, and it is unlawful for any person or persons to enter the waters of the pools except when the managers or lifeguards are in charge of the same and on duty.
(History: Ord. SP-829 §2, 75; SP-518 §10, 68)

heading: 10.04.090 Charges to Be Fixed by City Manager.
text:
The charges for public use of the swimming pools shall be fixed by the City Manager pursuant to the Parks and Recreation Fee and Cost Recovery Policy as adopted by the Governing Body and the City Manager or their designee may establish any and all policies or waivers related to the same.
(History: Ord. P-3399, §1, 2023; Ord. SP-518 §11, 68)

heading: 10.04.100 Making and Enforcing Rules and Regulations - Posting.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation by and with the consent of the City Manager is authorized to make and enforce such additional rules and regulations as may be necessary for the management and operation of the swimming pools. Copies of all rules shall be posted in conspicuous places about the swimming pools as may be determined by the Director of Parks and Recreation.
(History: Ord. SP-829 §3, 75; SP-518 §12, 68)

heading: 10.04.130 Guests - Number Allowed.
text:
The pool managers of the Overland Park swimming pools shall have the authority to limit admittance of guests into the swimming pools whenever, in their opinion, the pools are so crowded as to make it unsafe for the safety of the people to permit them. The managers shall, in addition, have authority to designate pool areas which guests and/or residents may use.
(History: Ord. SP-518 §15, 68)

heading: 10.04.140 Revocation of Swimming Privileges and Suspension of Membership.
text:
It is unlawful for any person or persons to violate the lawful orders of the Director of Parks & Recreation and/or the designated supervisor within the swimming pool area of the City park, and any person or persons who violate such order or orders shall forfeit their right to swimming privileges at the pool or pools and the pool manager may suspend the use and membership for a period not to exceed seven days. A suspension of greater than seven days may be recommended to the Aquatic Supervisor or Assistant Aquatic Supervisor, the recommendation will be reviewed and investigated and then affirmed or overruled. Memberships that have been suspended for a period of greater than seven days may make application for their return through the City Clerk's office, and the City Manager of the City shall, after investigation, affirm or overrule the suspension of the person or person's swimming privileges. Any person aggrieved of the decision of the City Manager may appeal to the Council.
(History: Ord. SP-2709 §1, 2008; SP-518 §16, 68)

heading: 10.04.150 Violation - Penalties.
text:
Any person or persons violating any of the provisions of this chapter declared to be unlawful, shall upon conviction thereof, be punished as provided in 1.12.010; provided, that the penalties herein prescribed shall not affect the provisions of 10.04.140.
(History: Ord. SP-518 §17, 68)

heading: 10.06.010 When Open.
text:
The municipal golf courses of the City shall be opened to the public as limited to this chapter at all proper and reasonable times subject to such rules and regulations contained in this chapter and as the Governing Body of the City may from time to time adopt or authorize.
(History: Ord. GC-825 §1, 75)

heading: 10.06.020 Golf Course Superintendent and Employees-Duties Generally.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation with consent of the City Manager, shall appoint a Golf Course Superintendent and other employees of the golf courses. The Golf Course Superintendent shall have general supervision over the golf courses and over all people attending the same and the park areas in which the same are located. It shall be his duty to preserve order, to enforce all provisions of this chapter and the rules and regulations of the City.
(History: Ord. GC-825 §2, 75)

heading: 10.06.030 Golf Professionals and Employees - Duties and Responsibilities Generally.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation shall with consent of the City Manager, and with the approval of the Governing Body of the City, contract with a Golf Professional for operation of a municipal golf course, clubhouse concessions, and related facilities. The Director of Parks and Recreation shall have general contract supervision responsibilities over the Golf Professional and his employees.
(History: Ord. GC-825 §3, 75)

heading: 10.06.040 When Admittance May Be Refused.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation is authorized, directed and empowered to refuse admission to any person applying for admission to the golf course, who is known to be intoxicated, under the influence of drugs or opiates, or not participating in golf related activities; and he may, when deemed to be in the best interest of orderly operation and management of the golf courses, refuse admission to any person or persons whatsoever.
(History: Ord. GC-825 §4, 75)

heading: 10.06.050 Fees to be Fixed by City Manager.
text:
The fees for public use of the municipal golf courses shall be fixed by the City Manager to the Parks and Recreation Fee and Cost Recovery Policy as adopted by the Governing Body and the City Manager or their designee may establish any and all policies or waivers related to the same.
(History: Ord. P-3399 §2, 2023; Ord. GC-2944 §1, 2012; GC-825 §5, 75)

heading: 10.06.060 Making and Enforcing Rules and Regulations, Definitions, and Procedures - Posting.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation is authorized to make and enforce the following:
1.
Golf Course Rules and Regulations
2.
Rules and Regulations for Riding Carts and Pullcarts
3.
Definitions
4.
Golf Course Operating Procedures
5.
Procedure for High School and College Golf Team Competition
6.
Procedure for Tournament and League Competition
7.
Procedure for Tournament and League Competition by the Overland Park and St. Andrews Golf Associations
The Director of Parks and Recreation is authorized to make and enforce any additions or changes to the above Rules and Regulations, Definitions, or Procedures as may be necessary for the management and operation of the golf courses. Copies of all the above Rules and Regulations, Definitions, and Procedures shall be posted in conspicuous places about the golf course clubhouse as may be determined by the Director of Parks and Recreation.
(History: Ord. GC-825 §6, 75)

heading: 10.06.070 Revocation of Golf Privileges.
text:
It is unlawful for any person or persons to violate the orders of the Director of Parks and Recreation and/or his designated supervisors within the golf course area of the City park, and any person or persons who violate such order or orders shall forfeit their right to golfing privileges at the municipal golf courses. Any person or persons denied golfing privileges under the provisions of this section may make application for reinstatement through the City Clerk's office, and the City Manager of the City, after investigation, affirm or overrule the suspension of the person or persons golfing privileges. Any person aggrieved of the decision of the City Manager may appeal such suspension to the Governing Body.
(History: Ord. GC-825 §7, 75)

heading: 10.06.080 Violation - Penalties
text:
Any person or persons violating any of the provisions of this chapter declared to be unlawful, shall upon conviction thereof, be punished as provided in 1.12.010 of the Overland Park Municipal Code; provided that the penalties herein prescribed shall not affect the provisions of 10.06.070.
(History: Ord. GC-825 §8, 75)

heading: 10.08.010 Hours.
text:
All parks owned and operated by the City shall be closed for use by the public between the hours of ten p.m. and five a.m.; provided, however, parks may be closed temporarily or opening hours extended temporarily in case of emergency, adverse weather conditions, or unusual circumstances as determined and ordered by the Director of Parks and Recreation.
(History: Ord. PR-830 §1, 75;PR-763 §1, 73)

heading: 10.08.020 Camping.
text:
Overnight camping on park property shall be allowed only by special permit issued to organized sponsored groups by the Director of Parks and Recreation. Special permits for overnight camping shall be issued for Indian Creek Camping Area only.
A "sponsored organized group" means any group or organization having local or national recognition and affiliation with organizations such as the Boy Scouts of America, the Girl Scouts of America, Cub Scouts, YMCA, Indian Guides and church groups.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §2, 73)

heading: 10.08.030 Camping Reservations.
text:
All requests for special permits as provided for in 10.08.020 shall be submitted to the Director of Parks and Recreation in letter form within 15 days of the desired date of reservation with the following information: Name of group, sponsoring agency, number in group, name and number of sponsors that will be present, designation of the park desired, designation of area to be utilized, and the inclusive dates of the reservation. No special permit shall be issued for more than three consecutive nights of camping. There shall be a minimum of one adult sponsor present for every ten members of the group. For purposes of this section "adult sponsor" is defined as a person 18 years of age or more.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §3, 73)

heading: 10.08.040 Picnic Shelter Reservations.
text:
All requests for reservations of picnic shelters shall be made by phone to the parks and recreation department at least seven days prior to the date requested. Notification of approval or denial of reservation shall be by mail. Groups of at least 20 persons and not more than 100 may reserve a picnic shelter.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §4, 73)

heading: 10.08.045 Athletic Fields, Courts, and Areas Reservations.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation shall establish rules and regulations for use of the athletic fields, courts, and areas. Any fees for use of athletic fields, courts, and areas shall be fixed by the City Manager pursuant to the Parks and Recreation Fee and Cost Recovery Policy as adopted by the Governing Body and the City Manager or their designee may establish any and all policies or waivers related to the same.
(History: Ord. P-3399 §3, 2023; Ord. PR-830 §2, 75)

heading: 10.08.050 Special Permit or Reservation Denial - Appeal.
text:
Any person aggrieved by the denial of a special permit or reservation under the provisions of this chapter may appeal to the City Council for a review by filing a notice of appeal with the City Clerk within ten days after receipt of such denial.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §5, 73)

heading: 10.08.060 Alcoholic Beverages. (Repealed)
text:
Repealed.
(History: Ord. POC-3367 §9, 2022; Ord. PR-2538 §1, 2005; PR-763 §6, 73)

heading: 10.08.070 Sanitation and Fires.
text:
All waste material and refuse of any kind shall be deposited in disposal drums provided for such purpose and no such waste or contaminating material shall be discarded otherwise in or upon park land.
Fires may be built only in the ovens, stoves or ring pits provided by the City and must be extinguished before leaving the area. Fires may be prohibited entirely as a protective measure from time to time by the posting by the City of special warning signs and may be part of the conditions upon which special permits or reservations are given.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §7, 73)

heading: 10.08.080 Swimming, Bathing and Wading
text:
Swimming, bathing and wading are prohibited except at such times and in such locations as are approved by the City.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §8, 73)

heading: 10.08.090 Hunting.
text:
No person shall pursue, catch, kill or take any wildlife except as provided in 10.08.100.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §9, 73)

heading: 10.08.100 Fishing and Frogging.
text:
Fish and game laws of the state of Kansas must be strictly observed while fishing at parks with the exception that the daily limit on Bluegill is set at 30 per fisherman, and no trotline, jug, blockline, gigging, seining, snaring, or snagging will be permitted at any time. This includes the requirement for all Kansas residents between the ages of 16 and 65 to have a Kansas State Fishing License. All non-residents of Kansas must have a state fishing license at 16 years of age or older.
For the purpose of interpretation of these rules, the word "fishing" and the word "frogging" are synonymous, wherever used.
(History: Ord. PR-1775 §1, 92; PR-763 §10, 73)

heading: 10.08.110 Skating.
text:
No person shall, at any time, skate except upon areas designated by the City and at such times and pursuant to such rules as the City has posted.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §11, 73)

heading: 10.08.120 Firecrackers or Fireworks.
text:
Firecrackers or fireworks are prohibited, except for fireworks displays on special events and then only as approved upon application to the City.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §12, 73)

heading: 10.08.130 Steering and Sailing Rules.
text:
Boats or crafts shall not be operated in a manner or at a speed greater than is safe and prudent under the circumstances, and the operator thereof shall observe all signs and directions placed on or near the lake and obey all orders and regulations of the City and its supervisory personnel. Boats with motors are prohibited.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §13, 73)

heading: 10.08.140 Water Safety.
text:
No boat or craft of any kind or character shall be operated on park waters unless it carries for each occupant a suitably designed life preserver in good condition and approved as adequate for that purpose, and every boat or craft of any kind or character shall have aboard oars of such size and number as required properly to operate the boat or craft. While a boat or craft is on the water each occupant shall properly wear a life jacket at all times.
No boat or craft may be used in racing or practicing therefor on park waters, except at such hours on such days as the City may from time to time specially designate therefor, and no boat shall be operated in such a manner as to endanger the lives or property of others.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §14, 73)

heading: 10.08.142 Domestic Animals.
text:
Domestic animals present within a park area shall be subject to the provisions of Title 6. The Director of Parks and Recreation may establish rules and regulations in addition thereto to prohibit such domestic animals from certain park areas to prevent damage and provide safe use of park areas. The Director of Parks and Recreation may establish certain park areas for use by owners of domestic animals for recreational purposes as dog and cat shows, bridal paths, and neighborhood circuses.
(History: Ord. PR-830 §3, 75)

heading: 10.08.144 Motor Vehicles - Cycles - Prohibited.
text:
A.
Motor vehicles are specifically prohibited from operation within any City parks or bike-hike trails,​​​​​​​ ​​​​​​​except for ​​​​​​​parking lots, parking ​​​​​​​access drives​​​​​​​, ​​​​​​​park streets, ​​​​​​​areas specifically established by the Director of Parks and Recreation for motor vehicle use, or as set forth in subsection B​​​​​​​. The presence of motor vehicles in parking lots, parking access drives, and park streets between the hours of 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. is prohibited. This prohibition includes, but is not limited to:
1.
Automobiles or trucks
2.
Mopeds or motorized scooters (electric or otherwise)
3.
Other motorized vehicles (electric or otherwise) such as golf carts, ATVs, motorcycles, autocycles, electric personal assistive mobility devices (e.g., segways), or other fuel-powered devices. ​​​​​​​
B.
Subject to regulation by the Director of Parks and Recreation, the following motor vehicles are allowed to be used on park trails and bike-hike trails:
1.
Electric-assisted scooters as defined in Section 12.04.001 of the Code.
2.
Electric-assisted bicycles as defined in Section 12.04.001 of the Code (including those commonly referred to as either Type 1 or Type 2 electric-assisted bicycles, which meet the definition of electric-assisted bicycle in Section 12.04.001 of the Code).
3.
Devices commonly referred to as, Type 3 electric-assisted ​​​​​bicycles, which is a bicycle with a throttle assisted motor that provides assistance only when rider is pedaling (pedal assist) and ceases when the bicycle reaches 28 miles per hour and is equipped with a speedometer.
4.
Any other form of electric powered mobility device approved by the Director of Parks and Recreation which is consistent with the above exempted devices.
5.
Motor vehicles used by the Overland Park Police Department in the course of an officer's official duties.
Provided, any allowed motor vehicle shall not exceed a maximum speed of 20 mph on any city trail.
(History: Ord. PR-3441 §1, 2023; ​​​​​​​Ord. PR-830 §4, 75)

heading: 10.08.146 Vandalism.
text:
It is unlawful for any person to commit an act of vandalism in a park area by willfully injuring, damaging, mutilating, defacing, destroying, or substantially impairing any park area or improvement within a park area.
(History: Ord. PR-830 §5, 75)

heading: 10.08.150 Commercial Uses.
text:
No park area may be used for any commercial enterprise in any form except wherein the City is directly involved as a co-sponsor of an event or project.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §15, 73)

heading: 10.08.160 Penalty for Violations.
text:
Violation of any provision of this chapter is a public offense and any person, firm, association, partnership or corporation convicted thereof shall be punished as provided in 1.12.010.
(History: Ord. PR-763 §16, 73)

heading: 10.08.170 Rules and Regulations.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation is hereby authorized to make and enforce such additional rules and regulations as may be necessary for the management and operation of any of the lands, buildings, structures or facilities that are placed under the supervision of the Director of Parks and Recreation by action of the Governing Body or the City Manager. This regulatory authority shall be supplementary to any specific such authority contained elsewhere in the Overland Park Municipal Code. Such rules and regulations shall have the force and effect of law and the violation of those rules shall constitute a public offense and shall be enforced in the same manner as other violations of the Municipal Code. Violation of any adopted rules and regulations shall be grounds for eviction from the park lands, buildings or facilities and the denial, revocation or suspension of any permit issued or privilege granted by the Parks and Recreation Department. These rules and regulations must be approved by the Director and either posted in a conspicuous place in or on the park lands, buildings structures or facilities or be maintained in written form and available to the public in the office of the Director of Parks and Recreation prior to their becoming effective.
(History: Ord. PR-2233 §1, 2000)

heading: 10.10.010 When Open - Rules and Regulations Generally.
text:
The community centers of the City shall be open to the public, as limited in this chapter, year round subject to such rules and regulations contained in this chapter and as the Governing Body of the City may from time to time adopt or authorize.
(History: Ord. CC-1529 §1, 88; CC-975 §1, 75)

heading: 10.10.020 Center Directors and Employees - Duties Generally.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation, with the consent of the City Manager, shall appoint center directors and other employees of the City's community centers. A center's director shall have general supervision over the community center and all people attending the same and the park areas in which the same are located. It shall be the center director's duty to preserve order, to enforce all provisions of this chapter, and the rules and regulations established by the City. The center director may exclude any person or persons from the center for violations of this chapter, such rules and regulations as may be made by the City, or when the center director deems such exclusion to be in the best interest of the orderly and peaceable operation and management of the community center.
(History: Ord. CC-1529 §2, 88; CC-975 §2, 78)

heading: 10.10.030 Requests for Use or Reservations - Fees.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation shall establish rules and regulations for use of community center rooms and/or facilities. Any fees for use of rooms and/or facilities shall be fixed by the City Manager pursuant to the Parks and Recreation Fee and Cost Recovery Policy as adopted by the Governing Body and the City Manager or their designee may establish any and all policies or waivers related to the same.
(History: Ord. P-3399 §4, 2023; Ord. CC-1529 §3, 88; CC-975 §3, 78)

heading: 10.10.040 Requests for Use or Reservation Denial - Appeal.
text:
Any person aggrieved by the denial of a special permit or reservation under the provisions of this chapter may appeal to the City Council for a review by filing notice of appeal with the City Clerk within 10 days after receipt of such denial.
(History: Ord. CC-1529 §4, 88; CC-975 §4, 78)

heading: 10.10.050 Commercial Uses.
text:
Repealed.
(History: Ord. CC-2022 §1, 97; CC-1529 §5, 88; CC-975 §5, 78)

heading: 10.10.060 Making and Enforcing Rules and Regulations - Posting.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation by and with the consent of the City Manager is authorized to make and enforce such additional rules and regulations as may be necessary for the management and operation of the City's community centers. Copies of all rules shall be posted in conspicuous places about the community center.
(History: Ord. CC-1529 §6, 88; CC-975 §6, 78)

heading: 10.12.010 When Open - Rules and Regulations Generally.
text:
The Overland Park Arboretum shall be open to the public, as limited in this chapter, year round subject to such rules and regulations contained in this chapter and as the Governing Body of the City may from time to time adopt or authorize.
(History: Ord. ABG-2205 §1, 2000)

heading: 10.12.020 Supervisors and Employees - Duties Generally.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation, with the consent of the City Manager, shall appoint supervisors and other employees of the Overland Park Arboretum. The Arboretum Supervisor shall have general supervision over the Arboretum and all people attending the same and the facilities located in the same. It shall be the supervisor's duty to preserve order, to enforce all provisions of this chapter, and the rules and regulations established by the City. The supervisor may exclude any person or persons from the Arboretum for violations of this chapter, such rules and regulations as may be made by the City, or when the supervisor deems such exclusion to be in the best interest of the orderly and peaceable operation and management of the Arboretum.
(History: Ord. ABG-2205 §1, 2000)

heading: 10.12.030 Fees.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation shall establish rules and regulations for use of the Arboretum and/or facilities. Any fees shall be fixed by the City Manager (through the Director of Parks and Recreation) pursuant to the Parks and Recreation Fee and Cost Recovery Policy as adopted by the Governing Body and the City Manager or their designee may establish any and all policies or waivers related to the same.
(History: Ord. P-3399 §5, 2023; Ord. ABG-2205 §1, 2000)

heading: 10.12.040 Requests for Use or Reservation Denial - Appeal.
text:
Any person aggrieved by the denial of a special permit or reservation under the provisions of this chapter may appeal to the City Council for a review by filing notice of appeal with the City Clerk within 10 days after receipt of such denial.
(History: Ord. ABG-2205 §1, 2000)

heading: 10.12.050 Commercial Uses.
text:
The City's Arboretum may not be used for any commercial enterprise in any form except wherein the City is directly involved as a co-sponsor of an event or project, or the commercial use has been approved and the appropriate fees submitted.
(History: Ord. ABG-2205 §1, 2000)

heading: 10.12.060 Making and Enforcing Rules and Regulations - Posting.
text:
The Director of Parks and Recreation by and with the consent of the City Manager is authorized to make and enforce such additional rules and regulations as may be necessary for the management and operation of the Overland Park Arboretum. Copies of all rules shall be posted in conspicuous places about the Arboretum.
(History: Ord. ABG-2205 §1, 2000)

text:

heading: 11.04.020 Civil Remedies Preserved.
text:
This title does not bar, suspend or otherwise affect any civil right or remedy, authorized by law to be enforced in a civil action, based on conduct which it makes punishable.

heading: 11.04.260 Public Offenses - Penalties.
text:
A.
It is unlawful for any person to commit any of the offenses hereinafter described in this title, including that certain code known as the Uniform Public Offense Code, 42nd Edition, prepared and published in book form by the League of Kansas Municipalities, Topeka, Kansas, hereby incorporated by reference, and any person so offending is guilty of a public offense and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished as set forth herein.
B.
Classes of violations and confinement.
For the purpose of sentencing, the following classes of public offense violations and the punishment and the terms of confinement authorized for each class are established:
1.
Persons convicted of a class A violation shall be sentenced to a definite term of confinement in the city or county jail which shall be fixed by the court and shall not exceed one year.
2.
Persons convicted of a class B violation shall be sentenced to a definite term of confinement in the city or county jail which shall be fixed by the court and shall not exceed six months.
3.
Persons convicted of a class C violation shall be sentenced to a definite term of confinement in the city or county jail which shall be fixed by the court and shall not exceed one month.
4.
Unclassified violations, which shall include all offenses without specification as to class, the sentence for which shall be in accordance with the sentence specified in the section that defines the offense; if no penalty is provided in such section, the penalty shall be the same penalty as provided herein for a class C violation.
C.
Upon conviction of a violation, a person may be punished by a fine, as provided in paragraph F, instead of or in addition to confinement, as provided in this section.
D.
In addition to or in lieu of any other sentence authorized by law, whenever there is evidence that the act constituting the violation was substantially related to the possession, use or ingestion of cereal malt beverage or alcoholic liquor by such person, the court may order such person to attend and satisfactorily complete an alcohol or drug education or training program certified by the chief judge of the judicial district or licensed by the secretary of aging and disability services.
E.
Whenever there is evidence that the act constituting a violation was motivated in whole or in part by bias as described below, the following mandatory minimum sentences shall apply, unless other mandatory minimum sentences are applicable:
1.
Upon a first conviction of one of the crimes set forth in paragraph E(3) below, and a showing of any motive or intent relating to, or any antipathy, animosity or hostility based upon the race, color, gender, religion, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, ancestry, disability or handicap of another individual or group of individuals, a person shall be punished by a fine of no less than five hundred dollars ($500) of which all or a portion may be suspended during a period of probation or parole, and/or no less than six (6) months in jail, which sentence may be suspended during a period of probation or parole.
2.
Upon a second conviction of one of the crimes set forth in paragraph E(3) below, and a showing of any motive or intent relating to, or any antipathy, animosity or hostility based upon the race, color, gender, religion, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, ancestry, disability or handicap of another individual or group of individuals, a person shall be punished by a fine of no less than five hundred dollars ($500) of which a minimum of two hundred and fifty dollars ($250) shall be assessed; all or a portion of the balance may be suspended during a period of probation or parole, and/or no less than six (6) months in jail, which sentence may be suspended during a period of probation or parole, but only after such person has served a minimum of three (3) days in jail.
3.
Mandatory minimum penalties outlined in E(1) and (2) above shall apply to the following crimes, contained within that certain code known as the Uniform Public Offense Code, 42nd Edition, prepared and published in book form by the League of Kansas Municipalities, Topeka, Kansas, hereby incorporated by reference, or otherwise adopted in the Overland Park Municipal Code:
a.
Battery (UPOC 3.1);
b.
Criminal Damage to Property (UPOC 6.6);
c.
Criminal Trespass (UPOC 6.7);
d.
Harassment by Telecommunication Device (UPOC 9.1);
e.
Criminal Carrying of a Weapon (UPOC 10.1.1);
f.
Unlawful Discharge of Firearms (OPMC 11.60.072)
4.
Upon a first conviction of one of the crimes set forth in paragraph E(6) below, and a showing of any motive or intent relating to, or any antipathy, animosity or hostility based upon the race, color, gender, religion, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, ancestry, disability or handicap of another individual or group of individuals, a person shall be punished by a fine of no less than five hundred dollars ($500) of which all or a portion may be suspended during a period of probation or parole, and/or no less than one (1) month in jail, which sentence may be suspended during a period of probation or parole.
5.
Upon a second conviction of one of the crimes set forth in paragraph E(6) below, and a showing of any motive or intent relating to, or any antipathy, animosity or hostility based upon the race, color, gender, religion, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, ancestry, disability or handicap of another individual or group of individuals, a person shall be punished by a fine of no less than five hundred dollars ($500) of which a minimum of two hundred and fifty dollars ($250) shall be assessed; all or a portion of the balance may be suspended during a period of probation or parole, and/or no less than one (1) month in jail, which sentence may be suspended during a period of probation or parole, but only after such person has served a minimum of three (3) days in jail.
6.
Mandatory minimum penalties outlined in E(4) and (5) above shall apply to the following crimes contained within that certain code known as the Uniform Public Offense Code, 42nd Edition, prepared and published in book form by the League of Kansas Municipalities, Topeka, Kansas, hereby incorporated by reference:
a.
Assault (UPOC 3.3);
b.
Disorderly Conduct (UPOC 9.1)
F.
Fines.
1.
A person convicted of a public offense violation may, in addition to or instead of the confinement set forth in paragraph B above, be sentenced to pay a fine which shall be fixed by the court as follows:
a.
Class A violation, a sum not exceeding $2,500.
b.
Class B violation, a sum not exceeding $1,000.
c.
Class C violation, a sum not exceeding $500.
d.
Unclassified violation, any sum authorized by the section that defines the offense or if no penalty is provided in such law, the fine shall not exceed the fine provided herein for a class C violation.
2.
As an alternative to any of the above fines, the fine imposed may be fixed at any greater sum not exceeding double the pecuniary gain derived from the crime by the offender.
(History: Ord. POC-3529, §3, 2026; Ord. POC-3460 §3, 2024; Ord. POC-3423 §3, 2023; POC-3269 §1, 2019; Ord. POC-2055 §1, 97; POC-1986 §1, 96; POC- 1381 §1, 86) (State Law: K.S.A. 21-4502 and K.S.A. 21-4503a)

heading: 11.12.060 Criminal Littering.
text:
Except as provided in Section 112.1 of the Standard Traffic Ordinance, 52nd Edition, prepared and published in book form by the League of Kansas Municipalities, Topeka, Kansas, criminal littering is intentionally or recklessly depositing or causing to be deposited any object or substance into, upon or about:
A.
Any public street, highway, alley, road, right-of-way, park or other public place, or any lake, stream, watercourse, or other body of water, except by direction of some public officer or employee authorized by law or ordinance to direct or permit such acts; or
B.
Any private property without the consent of the owner or occupant of such property.
C.
Upon a first conviction, a fine shall be imposed of no less than $250 nor more than $1,000; upon a second conviction, a fine shall be imposed of no less than $1,000 nor more than $2,000; and upon a third or subsequent conviction, a fine shall be imposed of no less than $2,000 nor more than $4,000. In addition to any fines imposed pursuant to this subsection, a person convicted of littering shall be required to pick up litter for a time prescribed by and a place within the city limits of Overland Park, Kansas.
(History: Ord. POC-3505 §1, 2026; Ord. POC-2499 §2, 2004; POC-1801 §7, 93; POC-625 §31, 72; POC-598 §31)(State Law: K.S.A. 21-5815)

heading: 11.12.155 Unlawful Hunting.
text:
A.
It shall be unlawful for any person to shoot or hunt any animal or bird within the City unless that person:
1.
Is in possession of a valid Kansas hunting license or other permit authorizing the taking of wildlife, or is exempted from possessing a hunting license by the State of Kansas; and
2.
Is hunting on land that is primarily rural or devoted to agricultural use; and
3.
Is in possession of the written permission of the landowner where the hunting is occurring; and
4.
When hunting with a firearm, is in possession of the written permission of all landowners or persons in possession of land contiguous to the land where the hunting is occurring when on land that contains less than 40 acres; and
5.
When hunting with a bow, is in possession of the written permission of all landowners or persons in possession of land contiguous to the land where the hunting is occurring when on land that contains less than 30 acres; and
6.
Utilizes a shotgun with shot shells containing pellets of 00 buckshot or smaller shot, or utilizes a rifle or pistol with a bore diameter of .224 caliber or less and the ammunition is of rim fire configuration.
B.
It shall be unlawful for any person, unless authorized by special permit issued by the State of Kansas to hunt by:
1.
Taking any game animal or furbearing animal from a motorboat, airplane, motor vehicle or other water, air or land vehicle unless such person holds a valid handicapped hunting and fishing permit.
2.
Providing or receiving information concerning the location of any game animal or furbearing animal by radio or other mechanical device for purposes of taking such bird or animal.
3.
Using sodium fluoroacetate, commonly called formula 1080, except as permitted by rules and regulations of the Secretary of Wildlife and Parks of the State of Kansas.
4.
Using poison, poisonous gas, smoke or ferrets, or any smoke gun or other device for forcing smoke or any other asphyxiating or deadly gas or liquid into the holes, dens, runways, or houses of wildlife, except as permitted by rules and regulations of the Secretary of Wildlife and Parks of the State of Kansas.
5.
Throwing or casting the rays of a spotlight, headlight or other artificial light on any highway, or in any field, grassland, woodland, or forest for the purpose of spotting, locating or taking any animal, except furbearing animals when treed with the aid of dogs, while having in possession or control either singly or as one of a group of persons, any rifle or pistol, shotgun, bow or other implement whereby wildlife could be taken.
6.
Utilizing a rifle or pistol having a bore diameter greater than .224 caliber and the ammunition must be of rim fire configuration, provided slugs in shotguns are permitted on land of more than 100 acres.
C.
It shall be unlawful for any person otherwise lawfully hunting within the City to discharge a firearm or other projectile within 500 feet of a residence, school, church, airport, cemetery, or public recreation facility to include all adjacent or contiguous property owned or used for such purposes.
D.
The provisions of this Section shall not apply to persons hunting on any property zoned RUR that is annexed into the City pursuant to Ordinance No. A-2719, unless and until such property is rezoned, subject to the following provisions:
1.
No one shall discharge any shotgun, muzzleloader, rimfire rifle, or any handgun within 200 yards of a building inhabited by people or within 200 yards of a feedlot unless the owner, if owner-occupied, or legal tenant, if tenant-occupied, of the building or feedlot has given written consent to do so. “Feedlot” shall mean any yard, enclosure or coral where livestock are confined for purposes of feeding and growth prior to slaughter. Pastures, hayfields, or cropfields where animals are allowed to graze are not deemed to be a “feedlot.”
2.
No one shall discharge a center-fire rifle except from an elevated stand or platform of not less than 10 feet above the ground surface, and no one shall discharge any center-fire rifle within 500 yards of a building inhabited by people or within 500 yards of a feedlot unless the owner, if owner-occupied, or legal tenant, if tenant-occupied, of the building or feedlot has given written consent to do so. “Feedlot” shall have the meaning given to it in the immediately preceding subsection.
(History: Ord. POC-2788 §2, 2008; POC-2729 §1, 2008, modified during codification under authority of K.S.A. 12-3015; POC-2403 §1, 2002; POC-1771 §1, 92; POC-1646 §1, 90; POC-1578 §1, 89; POC-1381 §3, 86; POC-625 §35, 72; POC-598 §34)

heading: 11.20.060 Obstructing Legal Process or Official Duty.
text:
Obstructing legal process or official duty is knowingly and willfully obstructing, resisting or opposing any person authorized by federal law, state law or city ordinance to serve process in the service or execution or in the attempt to serve or execute any writ, warrant, process or order of a court, administrative agency, body, person or office having authority to so act in compliance with federal, state or city laws, ordinances or regulations or in the discharge of any official duty provided that the mere utterance of oral communication, verbal expression or other forms of vocalizing the spoken word shall not be unlawful unless said utterance rises to the level of "fighting words." Every person convicted of violating this section shall be imprisoned for not more than one year or fined not to exceed $2,500, or both such fine and imprisonment.

heading: Alcohol
text:
A.
Alcohol means the product of distillation of any fermented liquid, whether rectified or diluted, whatever its origin, and includes synthetic ethyl alcohol but does not include denatured alcohol or wood alcohol. (See K.S.A. 41-102(a))

heading: Alcoholic liquor
text:
C.
Alcoholic liquor means alcohol, spirits, wine, beer, alcoholic candy and every liquid or solid, patented or not, containing alcohol, spirits, wine, or beer and capable of being consumed by a human being, but shall not include any cereal malt beverage. (See K.S.A. 41-102(c))

heading: Beer
text:
D.
Beer, when its meaning is not enlarged, modified, or limited by other words, means a beverage, containing more than 3.2% alcohol by weight, obtained by alcoholic fermentation of an infusion or concoction of barley, or other grain, malt and hops in water and includes beer, ale, stout, lager beer, porter and similar beverages having such alcoholic content. (See K.S.A. 41-102(d))
1.
Low-alcohol beer means beer containing not more than 6% alcohol by volume.

heading: Cereal malt beverage
text:
F.
Cereal malt beverage means any fermented but undistilled liquor brewed or made from malt or from a mixture of malt or malt substitute or any flavored malt beverage, as defined in K.S.A. 2020 Supp. 41-2729, and amendments thereto but does not include any such liquor which is more than 3.2% alcohol by weight. (See K.S.A. 41-2701(a))

heading: Intoxicating Liquors
text:
N.
Intoxicating Liquors as used in this chapter shall mean any alcoholic liquor or cereal malt beverage as defined herein.

heading: Legal age
text:
O.
Legal age for consumption of intoxicating liquor means 21 years of age. (See K.S.A. 41-2701(h))

heading: Person
text:
Q.
Person includes individuals, firms, partnerships, corporations, trusts and associations.

heading: Spirits
text:
R.
Spirits means any beverage which contains alcohol obtained by distillation, mixed with water or other substance in solution, and includes brandy, rum, whiskey, gin or other spirituous liquors, and such liquors when rectified, blended or otherwise mixed with alcohol or other substances. (See K.S.A. 41-102(ii))

heading: Wine
text:
S.
Wine means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the normal alcoholic fermentation of the juice of sound, ripe grapes, fruits, berries or other agricultural products, including such beverages containing added alcohol or spirits or containing sugar added for the purpose of correcting natural deficiencies. The term “wine” shall include hard cider and any other product that is commonly known as a subset of wine. (See K.S.A. 41-102(ll))

heading: 11.48.110 Persons under 21 Years of Age - Possession, Consumption and Receiving Intoxicating Liquor - Prohibited.
text:
A.
No person under the age of 21 shall possess, consume, obtain, purchase or attempt to obtain or purchase any intoxicating liquor except as authorized by law.
B.
This Section shall not apply to the possession and consumption of cereal malt beverage by a person under the age of 21 when the possession and consumption are permitted and supervised and the beverage is furnished by the person's parent or legal guardian.
C.
Provided further, this Section shall not prohibit any person 18 or over from serving intoxicating liquor as permitted by K.S.A. 41-308a, 41-308b, 41-727a, 41-2610, 41-2652, 41-2704 or 41-2727, and amendments thereto, and subject to any rules and regulations adopted pursuant to such statutes.
D.
Any person who is convicted of a violation of this Section or diverted in lieu of further criminal proceedings shall be required to submit to and complete an alcohol and drug evaluation by a community-based alcohol and drug safety action program certified pursuant to K.S.A. 8-1008 and amendments thereto and to pay a fee for such evaluation.
E.
Violations of this Section is a class C violation and shall be punishable by a fine of not less than $200.00 and not more than $500.00. In addition, the Court may assess a jail sentence of not more than thirty days.
F.
In addition to any other penalty provided for a violation of this section,
1.
The court may order the offender to do either or both of the following:
a.
Perform 40 hours of public service; or
b.
Attend and satisfactorily complete a suitable education or training program dealing with the effects of alcohol or other chemical substances when ingested by humans; and
2.
Upon a first conviction of a violation of this Section, the court shall order the division of vehicles to suspend the driving privileges of such offender for 30 days. Upon receipt of the court order, the division shall notify the violator and suspend the driving privileges of the violator for 30 days whether or not the person has a driver’s license.
3.
Upon a second conviction of a violation of this Section, the court shall order the division of vehicles to suspend the driving privileges of such offender for 90 days. Upon receipt of the court order, the division shall notify the violator and suspend the driving privileges of the violator for 90 days whether or not the person has a driver’s license.
4.
Upon a third or subsequent conviction of a violation of this Section, the court shall order the division of vehicles to suspend the driving privileges of such offender for one year. Upon receipt of the court order, the division shall notify the violator and suspend the driving privileges of the violator for one year whether or not the person has a driver’s license.
G.
A law enforcement officer may request a person under 21 years of age to submit to a preliminary screening test of the person's breath to determine if alcohol has been consumed by such person if the officer has reasonable grounds to believe that the person has alcohol in the person's body except that, if the officer has reasonable grounds to believe the person has been operating or attempting to operate a vehicle under the influence of alcohol, the provisions of K.S.A. 8-1012, and amendments thereto, shall apply. No waiting period shall apply to the use of a preliminary breath test under this subsection. If the person submits to the test, the results shall be used for the purpose of assisting law enforcement officers in determining whether to charge a violation of this Section. A law enforcement officer may charge a person based in whole or in part upon the results of a preliminary screening test. Such results or a refusal to submit to a preliminary breath test shall be admissible in court in any criminal action, but are not per se proof that the person has violated this Section. The person may present to the court evidence to establish the positive preliminary screening test was not the result of a violation of this Section.
H.
A person and, if applicable, one or two other persons acting in concert with such person are immune from criminal prosecution for a violation of this Section prohibiting the acts prohibited by this Section, if such person:
1.
(a) Initiated contact with law enforcement or emergency medical services and requested medical assistance on such person’s behalf because such person reasonably believed such person was in need of medical assistance; and (b) cooperated with emergency medical services personnel and law enforcement officers in providing such medical assistance;
2.
(a) Initiated contact with law enforcement or emergency medical services, or was one of one or two other persons who acted in concert with such person, and requested medical assistance for another person who reasonably appeared to be in need of medical assistance; (b) provided their full name, the name of one or two other persons acting in concert with such person, if applicable, and any other relevant information requested by law enforcement or emergency medical services; (c) remained at the scene with the person who reasonably appeared to be in need of medical assistance until emergency medical services personnel and law enforcement officers arrived; and (d) cooperated with emergency medical services personnel and law enforcement officers in providing such medical assistance; or
3.
(a) Was the person who reasonably appeared to be in need of medical assistance as described in subsection H(2), but did not initiate contact with law enforcement or emergency medical services; and (b) cooperated with emergency medical services personnel and law enforcement officers in providing such medical assistance.
I.
A person shall not be allowed to initiate or maintain an action against a law enforcement officer, or the City, based on the officer’s compliance or failure to comply with subsection H.
(History: Ord. POC-3367 §2, 2022; Ord. POC-2751 §1, 2008; POC-2500 §1, 2004; POC-2311 §1, 2001; POC-2200 §1, 99; POC-1631 §2, 90; POC-1597 §1, 89; POC-1459 §2, 87; POC-1321 §2, 85; POC-625; POC-598) [Prior source of law: 5.12.120] (State Law: K.S.A. 41-727)

heading: 11.48.120 Furnishing Intoxicating Liquor to Persons under the Age of 21.
text:
A.
Furnishing intoxicating liquor to persons under the age of 21 is recklessly, directly or indirectly, buying for or distributing, any intoxicating liquor to any person under the legal age for consumption of intoxicating liquor.
B.
This section shall not apply to the furnishing of cereal malt beverage by a parent or legal guardian to such parent's child or such guardian's ward when such furnishing is permitted and supervised by the child's or ward’s parent or legal guardian.
C.
This Section shall not apply to wine intended for use and used by any church or religious organization for sacramental purposes.
D.
It shall be a defense to a prosecution under this Section if:
1.
The defendant is a licensed retailer, club, drinking establishment or caterer or holds a temporary permit, or an employee thereof;
2.
The defendant sold the intoxicating liquor to the person under the age of 21 with reasonable cause to believe that such person was of legal age for consumption of intoxicating liquor; and
3.
To purchase the intoxicating liquor, the person exhibited to the defendant a driver's license, Kansas nondriver's identification card or other official or apparently official document, that reasonably appears to contain a photograph of the person under the age of 21 and purporting to establish that such person was of legal age for consumption of intoxicating liquor.
E.
Violation of this Section is a class B violation, for which a minimum fine is $200.00.
(History: Ord. POC-3367 §3, 2022; Ord. POC-2500 §2, 2004; POC-2200 §2, 99; POC-1801 §16, 93; POC-1631 §3, 90; POC-1459 §3, 87; POC-1321 §3, 85; CMB-1145 §5, 81; POC-625 §24; POC-598 §24; CMB-SM-179) (State Law: K.S.A. 21-5607)

heading: 11.48.125 Unlawfully Hosting Persons under the Age of 21 Consuming Intoxicating Liquors.
text:

If the court sentences the offender to perform community or public service work as a condition of probation, as described in O.P.M.C. Section 2.33.294(e)(10), the court shall consider ordering the offender to serve the community or public service at an alcohol treatment facility.

heading: 11.48.160 Intoxicating Liquor in Public Places - Unlawful Acts.
text:
Except as otherwise provided herein and in Section 106 of the Standard Traffic Ordinance, 53rd Edition, prepared and published in book form by the League of Kansas Municipalities, Topeka, Kansas and amendments thereto, it is unlawful for any person to sell, serve, dispense, drink or consume any intoxicating liquor in or upon any public street, road, highway, avenue, alley or sidewalk, public way, public or private parking lot, or upon any public property, or within any vehicle in or upon any such place. In addition, it is unlawful for any person to possess in any such place, any open container of intoxicating liquor. Provided, however:
A.
The Governing Body may authorize the sale and consumption of cereal malt beverages and low-alcohol beer on public property pursuant to a valid application being submitted to said body and when said body determines that such activity would not be detrimental to the health, safety, and morals of the community.
B.
Intoxicating liquor may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed in or on designated street, alley, road, highway, parking or sidewalk areas of a licensed premises if title to the public area lies with the City and the licensee has received authorization to expand the premises from Kansas Alcohol Beverage Control, has received authorization from the Governing Body pursuant to the provisions of O.P.M.C. Section 5.20.075, and amendments thereto, and the licensee is complying with the provisions of that Section.
C.
Intoxicating liquor may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed on the Corporate Woods Founder’s Park during the Jazz Festival and the July 4th celebration provided the sale, serving, dispensing and consumption shall be in accordance with the written standards approved by the Director, Parks and Recreation Services.
D.
Cereal malt beverages, beer and wine as those terms are defined in O.P.M.C. Section 11.48.100, and amendments thereto, may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed at the Overland Park Fire Training Facility located at 12401 Hemlock, Overland Park, Kansas, in conjunction with professional and social events authorized by the Director of the Overland Park Fire Training Facility.
E.
Intoxicating liquor may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed on the Sykes/Lady Overland Park Golf Complex, including the Westlinks Course, located at 12501 Quivira Road and the St. Andrews Golf Course located at 11099 W. 135th Street, Overland Park, Kansas, provided the sale, serving, dispensing and consumption of intoxicating liquor shall be in accordance with written standards approved by the Director, Parks and Recreation Services.
F.
Intoxicating liquor may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed on real property leased by the City to others under the provisions of K.S.A. 12-1740 through 12-1749, and amendments thereto, provided such real property is actually being used for hotel or motel purposes or purposes incidental thereto.
G.
Intoxicating liquor may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed on any property that is located within the corporate limits of the City and is under the control of the Kansas State Board of Regents and the Board of Regents has exempted said property from the provisions of K.S.A. 41-719, and amendments thereto, and the property is not being used for classroom instruction.
H.
Intoxicating liquor may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed on the premises of the Overland Park Arboretum, provided the sale, serving, dispensing and consumption of these beverages shall be in accordance with written standards approved by the Director, Parks and Recreation Services.
I.
Intoxicating liquor may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed on the land platted as Convention Center Plaza in the City of Overland Park, Kansas, in accordance with and to the extent allowed by the written standards relating to intoxicating liquor promulgated by the City Manager or the City Manager's designees.
J.
Cereal malt beverages, beer and wine may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed on the premises of the Kemper Farm Property, provided the sale, serving, dispensing and consumption of those beverages shall be in accordance with written standards approved by the Director, Parks and Recreation Services.
K.
Intoxicating liquor may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed at the City of Overland Park Community Centers, in accordance with written standards approved by the Director, Parks and Recreation Services.
L.
Intoxicating liquor may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed at the Deanna Rose Farmstead provided the sale, serving, dispensing and consumption shall be in accordance with written standards approved by the Director, Parks and Recreation Services.
M.
Intoxicating liquor may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed in the food court area at the Overland Park Soccer Complex provided the sale, serving, dispensing and consumption shall be in accordance with written standards approved by the Director, Parks and Recreation Services.
N.
Intoxicating liquor may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed within the boundaries of the Thompson Park in accordance with and to the extent allowed by the written standards approved by the Director, Parks and Recreation Services.
O.
Intoxicating liquor may be sold, served, dispensed and consumed on grounds of the downtown Clock Tower area and the Farmer's Market area provided the sale, serving, dispensing and consumption shall be in accordance with the written standards approved by the Director, Parks and Recreation Services.
P.
Consumption on public streets, alleys, roads, sidewalks or highways.
a.
Intoxicating liquor may be consumed on public streets, alleys, roads, sidewalks, parking areas, or highways when:
i.
A temporary permit has been issued pursuant to O.P.M.C. Section 5.20.078 and amendments thereto, for an event if the Governing Body has approved by ordinance or resolution the event and the consumption of intoxicating liquor on such public streets, alleys, roads, sidewalks, parking areas, or highways, provided: a) the Governing Body closes the streets, alley, road, sidewalk, parking areas, or highway to motor vehicle traffic during the event; b) the boundaries of any such event are clearly designated in any application for the event and are clearly designated in any approval granted by the Governing Body; and c) the boundaries of such event are clearly marked by signs, a posted map or other means which reasonably identify the area in which intoxicating liquor may be possessed or consumed at such event. (See K.S.A. 41-719(a)(2)(A) and K.S.A. 41-1201(f)(1))
1.
Drinking establishments that are immediately adjacent to, or located within the licensed premises of an event, for which a temporary permit has been issued and the consumption of intoxicating liquor on public property has been approved, may request that the drinking establishment's licensed premises be extended into and made a part of the licensed premises of the event for the duration of the temporary permit issued for such event. (See K.S.A. 41-1201(f)(2))
2.
Each licensee selling intoxicating liquor for consumption on the premises of an event for which a temporary permit has been issued shall be liable for violations of all laws governing the sale and consumption of intoxicating liquor. (See K.S.A. 41-1201(f)(3))
ii.
A licensed caterer selling, serving and dispensing intoxicating liquor on public property listed herein has received authorization from Kansas Alcohol Beverage Control and from the Governing Body pursuant to O.P.M.C. Section 5.20.136, and amendments thereto, and complies with the provisions of that Section. (See K.S.A. 41-719(a)(2)(B))
iii.
The Governing Body has adopted an ordinance or resolution pursuant to O.P.M.C. Section 5.20.075, and amendments thereto, extending the licensed premises into a street, alley, road, sidewalk, parking area, or highway that is closed to motor vehicle traffic at any time during which alcoholic liquor is to be sold or consumed. (See K.S.A. 41-719(a)(2)(C) and K.S.A. 41-2608(c))
b.
No person shall remove any intoxicating liquor from inside the boundaries of an event approved by the governing body, from the boundaries of a catered event, or from the extended licensed premises of a public venue, hotel, hotel caterer, club, drinking establishment caterer or drinking establishment. No intoxicating liquor may be consumed inside vehicles while on public streets, alleys, roads or highways at any time. (See K.S.A. 41-719(a)(3)-(a)(4))
Q.
Intoxicating liquor may be consumed within common consumption areas designated by the City on public streets, alleys, roads, sidewalks, parking areas, parking lots, or highways pursuant to Section 5.22, and amendments thereto, except that no intoxicating liquor may be consumed inside vehicles while on public streets, alleys, roads, parking areas, parking lots or highways within a common consumption area. Further, no person shall remove any intoxicating liquor from inside the boundaries of the common consumption area which shall be clearly marked using a physical barrier or a clearly apparent line of demarcation.
R.
Any person under the age of 21 who is convicted of a violation of this Section or diverted in lieu of further criminal proceedings shall be required to submit to and complete an alcohol and drug evaluation by a community-based alcohol and drug safety action program certified pursuant to K.S.A. 8-1008, and amendments thereto, and to pay a fee for such evaluation.

heading: 11.48.162 Prohibited Hours.
text:
No person shall permit the serving, mixing, or consumption of alcoholic liquor or cereal malt beverage on the premises of a club, drinking establishment, public venue, caterer, or temporary permit holder licensed under the provisions of K.S.A. 41-2601 et seq., or O.P.M.C. 5.20, between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 6:00 a.m. on any day of the week, except in the case of temporary permit holders, hours of service, mixing and consumption shall be as indicated on the temporary permit and in conformance with state law. In addition, no caterer, or any owner, officer or employee thereof, shall allow the serving, mixing, or consumption of alcoholic liquor or cereal malt beverage between the hours of 2:00 a.m. and 6:00 a.m. on any day an event is catered by such caterer. However, a hotel of which the entire premises is licensed as a drinking establishment or as a drinking establishment caterer may allow at any time the serving, mixing and consumption of alcoholic liquor and cereal malt beverage from a minibar in a guest room by guests registered to stay in such room, and guests of guests registered to stay in such room.

heading: 11.52.140 Purpose.
text:
It is the purpose of this Ordinance that the City promotes public health by decreasing citizen’s exposure to secondhand smoke and creates smoke free environments for workers and citizens through regulation in the work place and all public places.
(History: Ord. POC-2632 §1, 2008)

heading: 11.52.150 Definitions.
text: For the purposes of this Ordinance, the following words shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them by this paragraph:

heading: Employee
text:
Employee
Any person who performs services for an employer, with or without compensation.

heading: Employer
text:
Employer
A person, partnership, association, corporation, trust, or other organized group of individuals, including the City or any agency thereof, which utilizes the services of one (1) or more employees.

heading: Enclosed
text:
Enclosed
A space bound by walls (with or without windows) continuous from the floor to the ceiling and enclosed by doors, including, but not limited to, offices, rooms, all space therein screened by partitions, which do not extend to the ceiling or are not solid, “office landscaping” or similar structures and halls.

heading: Open Office Landscaping
text:
Open Office Landscaping
Indoor areas without permanent walls, or walls that are not floor to ceiling; open space such as waiting areas and atriums; cubicles and/or open desk seating areas.

heading: Place of Employment
text:
Place of Employment
Any enclosed area under the control of public or private employer which employees normally frequent during the course of employment, including, but not limited to, work areas, employee lounges and restrooms, conference and classrooms, employee cafeterias, hotel or motel sleeping rooms, private rooms in nursing homes, private meeting/conference rooms and halls not open to the general public while being used for private functions or located within private clubs and hallways. A private residence is not a “place of employment” unless it is used as a childcare, adult day care or health care facility.

heading: Public Place
text:
Public Place
Any enclosed area to which the public is invited or in which the public is permitted, including but not limited to, banks, educational facilities, health facilities, laundromats, public transportation facilities, reception areas, production and marketing establishments, retail service establishments, retail stores, theaters, and waiting rooms. A private residence is not a “public place.”

heading: Service Line
text:
Service Line
Any indoor line at which one (1) or more persons are waiting for or receiving service of any kind, whether or not such service involves the exchange of money.

heading: Smoking
text:
Smoking
Inhaling, exhaling, burning or carrying any lighted cigar, cigarette, pipe or other tobacco product, or use of an electronic or battery-powered vaporizer that simulates tobacco smoking by producing an aerosol that resembles smoke. "Smoking" shall also include the use of liquid nicotine, the active ingredient of the tobacco plant (nicotine), in liquefied form when introduced into the human body by nasal spray, ingestion, smoking or other means.
Effective on: 8/1/2016

heading: Sports Arena
text:
Sports Arena
Sports pavilions, gymnasiums, health spas, boxing arenas, swimming pools, roller and ice rinks, bowling alleys and other similar places where members of the general public assemble either to engage in physical exercise, participate in athletic competition, or witness sports events.
(History: Ord. POC-3125 §6, 2016; POC-3054 §4, 2014; POC-2632 §2, 2008)
Effective on: 8/1/2016

heading: 11.52.160 Prohibition of Smoking in Enclosed Places of Employment and all Enclosed Public Places.
text:
A.
Smoking shall be prohibited in all enclosed places of employment within the City.
B.
It shall be the responsibility of employers to provide a smoke-free workplace for all employees.
Each employer having any enclosed place of employment located within the City shall adopt, implement, make known and maintain, a written smoking policy which shall contain the following requirements:
Smoking shall be prohibited in all enclosed facilities within a place of employment without exception. This includes common work areas, auditoriums, classrooms, conference and meeting rooms, private offices, elevators, hallways, medical facilities, cafeterias, employee lounges, stairs, restrooms and all other enclosed facilities.
C.
The smoking policy shall be communicated to all employees within four (4) weeks of the adoption of this Ordinance.
D.
All employers shall supply a written copy of the smoking policy upon request to any existing or prospective employee.
E.
Smoking shall be prohibited in all enclosed public places within the City, including, but not limited to, the following places:
1.
Any vehicle of public transportation, including but not limited to buses, limousines for hire and taxicabs.
2.
Elevators.
3.
Restrooms.
4.
Libraries, educational facilities, childcare and adult day care facilities, museums, auditoriums, aquariums and art galleries.
5.
Any health care facility, health clinics or ambulatory care facilities, including but not limited to laboratories associated with the rendition of health care treatment, hospitals, nursing homes, doctors' offices and dentists' offices.
6.
Any indoor place of entertainment or recreation, including but not limited to gymnasiums, theaters, concert halls, bingo halls, billiard halls, betting establishments, bowling alleys, arenas and swimming pools.
7.
Service lines.
8.
Facilities primarily used for exhibiting a motion picture, stage, drama, lecture, musical recital, or other similar performance; provided, however, that smoking may take place on stage during live theatrical performances, where smoking is integral to the plot or storyline and prior notice is given to the audience.
9.
Shopping malls.
10.
Sports arenas, including enclosed places in outdoor arenas.
11.
Bars.
12.
Restaurants.
13.
Convention facilities.
14.
All public areas and waiting rooms of public transportation facilities, including but not limited to bus and airport facilities.
15.
Any other area used by the public or serving as a place of work, including open office landscaping.
16.
Every room, chamber, place of meeting or public assembly, including school buildings under the control of any board, council, commission, committee, including, but not limited to joint committees, or agencies of the City or any political subdivision of the state during such time as a public meeting is in progress, to the extent such place is subject to the jurisdiction of the City.
17.
All enclosed facilities owned by the City.
18.
Rooms in which meetings or hearings open to the public are held, except where such rooms are in a private residence.
19.
Within 10 feet of any public entrance to a public place; provided, however, that this prohibition shall not apply to the following: any portion of the public right of way that may be within 10 feet of said entrance, and the outdoor seating area of a restaurant or drinking establishment where smoking is allowed. With respect to said outdoor seating area, smoking may be allowed only if reasonable efforts are made to minimize the chance of smoke affecting the inside occupants of the establishment.
(History: Ord. POC-2632 §3, 2008)

heading: 11.52.170 Where Smoking is Not Regulated.
text:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this Ordinance to the contrary, the following areas shall not be subject to the smoking restrictions of this Ordinance:
A.
Private residences, not serving as enclosed places of employment or an enclosed public place.
B.
Enclosed retail establishments whose primary business is the sale of tobacco products. Provided, enclosed retail establishments whose primary business is the sale of tobacco products which are established after March 31, 2008, can only be located in a stand-alone building not attached to or part of any building devoted to other uses.
C.
Enclosed retail establishments whose primary business is the sale of electronic cigarettes, which shall include, but not be limited to, any electronic or battery-powered vaporizer that simulates tobacco smoking by producing an aerosol that resembles smoke, or any component thereof. Provided, enclosed retail establishments whose primary business is the sale of electronic cigarettes which are established after August 31, 2014, can only be located in a stand-alone building not attached to or part of any building devoted to other uses.
D.
That portion of a medical or clinical research facility constituting a separately ventilated, secure smoking room dedicated and used solely and exclusively for clinical research activities conducted in accordance with regulatory authority of the United States or the state of Kansas, as determined by the director of alcoholic beverage control of the department of revenue.
(History: Ord. POC-3097 §1, 2015; POC-3054 §5, 2014; POC-2632 §4, 2008)

heading: 11.52.180 Responsibilities of Proprietors, Owners and Managers.
text:
The person having control of a place, business, office or other establishment or activity subject to this Ordinance shall not knowingly permit, cause, suffer or allow any person to violate the provisions of this Ordinance in that place and shall take all necessary steps to prevent or stop another person from smoking in violation of this Ordinance. Necessary steps means to take all reasonable actions to prevent smoking in violation of this Ordinance by employees, patrons and visitors in the place, business, office or establishment, including: posting no-smoking signs and removing all ashtrays; verbally asking a person who is smoking to extinguish the smoking materials; refusing service to a person who is illegally smoking; verbally asking anyone illegally smoking to leave the premises; and applying standard business procedures in the same manner for violations of house rules or other local ordinances or state laws. If the employee, patron or visitor smoking in violation of this Ordinance is hard of hearing, the communications with that person may be written, in sign language or other effective means of communication.
(History: Ord. POC-2632 §5, 2008)

heading: 11.52.190 Penalty for Violation of Ordinance.
text:
A.
A person who smokes in an area where smoking is prohibited by the provisions of this Ordinance shall be guilty of a public offense, punishable by a fine not exceeding fifty dollars ($50).
B.
A person having control of a public place or place of employment and who fails to comply with the provisions of this Ordinance shall be guilty of a public offense, punishable by:
1.
A fine not exceeding one hundred dollars ($100) for a first violation.
2.
A fine not exceeding two hundred dollars ($200) for a second violation within one (1) year.
3.
A fine not exceeding five hundred dollars ($500) for each additional violation within one (1) year.
C.
Each day on which a violation of this Ordinance occurs shall be considered a separate and distinct violation.
D.
In addition to the fines established by this Section, violation of this Ordinance by a person having control of a public place or place of employment may result in the suspension or revocation of any permit or license issued to the person for the premises on which the violation occurred.
(History: Ord. POC-2632 §6, 2008)

heading: 11.52.210 Severability.
text:
If any section, subsection, paragraph, sentence, clause or phrase in this chapter or any part thereof is for any reason held to be unconstitutional or invalid or ineffective by any court of competent jurisdiction, such decision shall not affect the validity or effectiveness of the remaining portions of this chapter or any part thereof.
